system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: the agent is provided with a list of available action types, guidelines for operating the phone, and a list of UI elements derived from the Android accessibility tree's leaf nodes
system_prompt_style.note: Prompt assembled from fixed guidelines plus per-step goal/UI elements; m3a.py not shown in evidence.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The observation space consists of a full-resolution screenshot and a UI tree representation developed for accessibility purposes.
env_context_strategy.note: Agent perceives current screen each step and acts; no repository/document retrieval.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: We request the agent to provide a concise summary of this step, including the intended action, success or failure, potential reasons for failure, and recommendations for subsequent actions. This summary will serve as the action history

observation_format.evidence_quote: The agent receives the current screenshot and a Set-of-Mark (SoM) (Yang et al., 2023a) annotated screenshot, which includes bounding boxes with numeric labels

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: M3A generates an action, represented in JSON, and reasoning for that action.

tool_count.note: Counted action types enumerated in random_agent action_weights (click, double_tap, scroll, swipe, navigate_home, navigate_back, keyboard_enter, wait, input_text); M3A's full action list (also answer, open_app, long_press, status) not in evidence.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: The action space is similar to that which humans use, consisting of gestures (i.e., tapping, swiping), typing, and navigation buttons

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: the agent is provided with a list of available action types, guidelines for operating the phone
tool_schema_source.note: Action space described in hand-written prompt text; JSONAction defined in code.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: selecting one of the [supported actions](https://github.com/google-research/android_world/blob/main/android_world/env/json_action.py), executing it through the AndroidEnv
protocol_standardization.note: No MCP/A2A in file tree or README.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: integrating ReAct-style (Yao et al., 2022) and Reflexion-style (Shinn et al., 2023) prompting to consume user instructions and screen content, reason, take actions

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: recommendations for subsequent actions. This summary will serve as the action history and be used for future action selection.

delegation_mechanism.note: Single agent stepped in loop; no delegation path.

human_in_loop.note: HumanAgent replaces the model rather than gating it.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: This summary will serve as the action history and be used for future action selection.
short_term_state.note: History of step summaries is the working state.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: It is zero-shot, integrating ReAct-style (Yao et al., 2022) and Reflexion-style (Shinn et al., 2023) prompting

state_persistence.evidence_quote: If a run fails part-way through, you can resume it by re-running the script with the `--checkpoint_dir` flag pointing to the output directory from the original run.
state_persistence.note: Suite-level checkpointing (checkpointer.py), not mid-episode agent state.

self_verification.evidence_quote: After executing an action, M3A reflects on its effect by observing any state changes that may have occurred.
self_verification.note: test_execution = harness reward check via task.is_successful(env) at episode end (minimal_task_runner.py:112); reward is not fed back to agent.

retry_policy.note: One episode per task instance; no retry loop.

rollback.note: Reset occurs between episodes (task setup/teardown), not as in-run rollback.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: run until it determines a task is complete, if the max number of steps is reached, of if the termination_fn is True.
termination_condition.note: termination_fn (e.g. nonzero MiniWoB reward) also ends the episode.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: For serious usage, you can switch to a more cost-effective model, by modifying the `model_name` in the script.
cost_controls.note: No token budget, caching or routing found; step budget is the only limit.

timeouts.evidence_quote: max_n_steps: The max number of steps to allow an agent to run before ending an episode.
timeouts.note: Only a step cap in the run loop; transition_pause is a sleep, not a timeout.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: It runs on a live Android emulator and contains a highly reproducible benchmark of 116 hand-crafted tasks across 20 apps
execution_isolation.note: Android Emulator (AVD); experimental Docker wrapper also shipped.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: With adb, A NDROID WORLD has complete access to system resources including the file system, application databases, and system settings.

network_policy.evidence_quote: **Open environment** with access to millions of Android apps and websites

permission_model.note: Actions executed directly, no authorisation layer.

tracing.note: Per-step step_data dicts collected into EpisodeResult and checkpointed.

replayability.evidence_quote: We set the seed to 30 and the temperature to 0 to aid reproducibility.
replayability.note: Seeded task parameterization; no trajectory replay module.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: each task includes dedicated initialization, success-checking, and tear-down logic, which modifies and inspects the device's system state.
eval_hooks.note: run.py + suite_utils.py evaluate the agent on the benchmark.

guardrails.note: No filters or action policies found in the run loop or env interface evidence.

target_domain.evidence_quote: AndroidWorld is an environment for building and benchmarking autonomous computer control agents.

open_source.evidence_quote: Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We use Gemini 1.5 Pro, GPT-4 Turbo, and the open-source Gemma 2 27B (Team et al., 2024) as base models.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: ANDROID WORLD and the experiments in this paper are available at https://github.com/google-research/android_world.

first_release_date.note: No tags in evidence; basis is arXiv v1 identifier 2405 (May 2024); exact date uncertain.
